speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been occurring?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the relief of discomfort after voiding and the presence of dyspareunia are significant clues. To differentiate between interstitial cystitis, a UTI, or pelvic floor dysfunction, do you notice any visible blood in your urine or burning sensation during urination?

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mention of painful intercourse alongside your bladder symptoms is significant; do you also experience lower back pain, fever, or any changes in the consistency of your vaginal discharge? Additionally, have you noticed any new growths or irregularities in your breasts or abdomen?

DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome with possible associated pelvic floor dysfunction.
